name: Typical Timeline for Soft-Story Seismic Retrofits in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: How long does a typical soft-story seismic retrofit take from first structural assessment through final inspection for a mid-sized Los Angeles County apartment building?
mainEntity.text: How long does a typical soft-story seismic retrofit take from first structural assessment through final inspection for a mid-sized Los Angeles County apartment building?

acceptedAnswer.text: The full timeline for a soft-story seismic retrofit in Los Angeles County is longer than the construction phase alone. For a mid-sized apartment building, owners should anticipate a 9–18 month process from first structural assessment to final sign-off in many cases. The initial structural evaluation and conceptual design often take 1–3 months, including site visits, engineering analysis, and preparation of preliminary plans. Plan development, coordination with ownership, and finalizing drawings suitable for permit submittal can add another 1–2 months. Permitting and plan check durations vary by jurisdiction and workload. Some cities and the County can complete reviews in a few months, while backlogs can push approvals to the 4–6 month range, especially if there are multiple rounds of comments. Once permits are issued, construction itself typically spans 2–6 months for a mid-sized building, depending on how many frames or walls are required, how constrained the site is, and how work is phased around tenant use of the property. Final inspections and corrections may add a few weeks at the end. Starting early in the compliance window, selecting a design team familiar with local ordinances, and submitting complete permit packages can help compress the timeline. Owners should build schedule float into financing and communication plans in case of review delays or unforeseen site conditions.
